motion.name: ease-out-quint

motion.name: press
motion.value: transform 150ms ease, background-color 150ms ease, border-color 150ms ease, color 150ms ease, box-shadow 150ms ease
motion.purpose: The `.press` utility: scale(0.98) on :active. Every tappable element carries it.

motion.name: stagger-item
motion.purpose: Screen entrance on the incumbent card routes via Stagger/StaggerItem.

motion.name: spine-draw
motion.value: 620ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), scaleY 0 to 1 from origin top
motion.purpose: Home-scoped, and Home's ONLY motion. The spine draws down and nothing else on the route animates; a per-section stagger here dilutes it.

motion.name: shake
motion.purpose: Rejected input on the set inputs.

narrative.overview:
Overload is a paper-white app with near-black ink and one electric lime. It reads like a plan written on a board in a training hall: the numbers are large enough to catch at arm's length, the labels that name them are small, tracked and uppercase, and the only colour carrying a decision is the lime on the thing you are meant to touch. The ground (#fafaf7) is warm off-white rather than pure white, so white surfaces sit above it without needing a shadow to prove it.

Density is honest rather than airy. Rows are compact (14px vertical), gutters are a single 22px inset, and the type ramp is steep — a 64px tabular numeral sits directly above a 10px label with nothing between them. Depth is mostly tonal: a border for things in a list, a soft shadow for things standing alone, never both on the same element. Dark surfaces are a distinct material, always carrying a 26px grid texture so black areas read as drafting paper rather than as a hole.

The system currently runs in two registers. Most screens compose in rounded cards (26px) on the off-white ground. Home was rebuilt to carry hierarchy in scale alone: no card, border, box or shadow on the route, structure held by hairline rules and a single vertical spine. That is Home-scoped. The rest of the app has not adopted it, and that inconsistency is known and accepted, not an oversight — do not migrate other screens toward Home without a decision to do so.
keyCharacteristics: Warm off-white ground, near-black ink, a single lime accent
One committed typeface (Outfit) doing display, body and label work
Tabular numerals everywhere a number can change
Dark surfaces always carry the 26px grid texture
Motion is short, quintic-eased, and always reduced-motion gated

rules.name: The One Lime Rule
rules.body: Lime marks the single thing you are meant to touch. Within a route's content it appears exactly once. The persistent chrome — the raised session button and the active-tab indicator — carries lime as well; that is chrome, and it is precisely why route content may never spend a second lime.

rules.name: The Data-Never-Acts Rule
rules.body: Muscle and session-type colour identifies data. It never becomes a button, a link or a primary surface. Lime never identifies data.

rules.name: The Muted Floor Rule
rules.body: ink-muted is the lightest text in the system. Anything lighter is decoration, not text.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Outfit is the committed face. A second family is not available to this system — if a register needs to feel different, translate it into Outfit through size, weight and tracking, as Home's 10px/0.14em label does.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that can change between renders is set in tabular numerals. Weights, reps, RPE, timers, streaks, counters, week indices.

rules.name: The Scale-Alone Rule (Home)
rules.body: On Home, hierarchy is carried by size, not by containers. The jump from a 64px value to its 10px caption is 6.4:1 and is load-bearing — nothing may be inserted between a value and its label to soften it.

rules.name: The Bordered-Or-Shadowed Rule
rules.body: A card is bordered when it lives in a list and shadowed when it stands alone. Never both on the same element.

rules.name: The Grid-Texture Rule
rules.body: Every dark surface carries the 26px grid texture. A flat black rectangle is not part of this system.

rules.name: The No-Container Rule (Home)
rules.body: Home has no card, border, box or shadow anywhere on the route. Anything that would have been a container is a rule instead. Home-scoped.

dos: Do take every colour, radius, shadow and easing from the @theme block in src/styles/index.css. Nothing downstream hardcodes a hex.
Do reserve lime for the single thing the user is meant to touch, and use accent-deep (#4e6011) whenever lime has to be read as text.
Do set every changeable number in tabular numerals.
Do give dark surfaces the 26px grid-texture.
Do choose bordered or shadowed for a card, based on whether it sits in a list or stands alone.
Do use ink-muted as the lightest text colour on anything new.
Do gate entrance motion on reduced-motion, and keep it to --ease-out-quint at 240-620ms.
Do put the section label above the card it names, at 11px/0.12em caps.
Do keep new routes on the incumbent card composition unless a decision is taken to migrate the app to Home's rule-and-spine structure.
donts: Don't use ink-faint (#8a8a82) for text. It measures 3.33:1 on the ground and fails the WCAG 2.2 AA bar this product commits to. KNOWN DRIFT: the shared .caps utility still hardcodes it, so every route except Home currently ships label text below the bar.
Don't add a second typeface. Translate the register into Outfit instead.
Don't put lime on a passive surface, and don't let a data colour (muscle or session type) become an action.
Don't put both a border and a shadow on the same card.
Don't introduce asymmetric or single-corner radii; the ladder is 6 / 12 / 14 / 22 / 26 / 999.
Don't add a per-section entrance stagger to Home — the spine draw is that route's only motion.
Don't put a card, border, box or shadow on Home, or a container radius on its action bar.
Don't carry Home's 10px/0.14em label register or its square spine marks onto other routes; they are Home-scoped until the app migrates deliberately.
